title: 6 Years of Savings from Mini-Split Heat Pump in Cold Climate
summary: Michigan homeowner reports six years of a single mini-split heat pump displacing a propane boiler, with running costs, sizing advice and service issues.

assertions.quote: it costs a lot of money to run the boiler though because it's on propane
that saved us five thousand seven hundred and forty eight dollars which is great considering we only paid forty one hundred dollars
in practicality it actually works down to about 9 degrees colder than that and it'll shut itself down
we do still have an operational boiler in the house that operates when it gets really really cold
you really need to have a qualified HVAC contractor do those calculations for you

verdicts.note: Field studies tie poor heat pump efficiency to bad sizing and emitter or flow design; a heat loss calculation is standard good practice.

assertions.quote: the bedrooms don't get quite the same temperature conditioning as the living room does

verdicts.note: A few wall heads heat open areas well but closed-off rooms lag, a common finding in ductless retrofits.
Ductless units were sized for the open living zone; closed-off back bedrooms in both homes were mainly heated by baseboards, so the mini-split covered only a fraction of the house.
Because a mini-split heats one or two rooms, homes with a single-zone furnace found it hard to use as the primary heat without underheating the rest of the house.

assertions.quote: the mini-split only costs an average of fifty seven dollars per month
